claims: Debtors are 'lodging tax returns that reconcile a full year of PAYG withholding against the FY2026-27 marginal repayment bands for the first time, with 15% charged only on income above $69,528' (repeated at line 16 key facts, line 27 'applies the FY2026-27 marginal bands', line 44-46 $80,000 example with $10,472 excess and ~$1,571, line 57 two jobs under $69,528).
'Millions of HECS debtors are lodging tax returns...'
whys: The article was published 2 July 2026. Returns lodged at tax time 2026 reconcile FY2025-26 income, where the marginal system's first year applied with a $67,000 threshold. FY2026-27 ($69,528) returns are not lodged until July 2027. On $80,000 the FY2025-26 excess is $13,000, so the repayment is about $1,950, not $1,571, and the $30/week STSL example no longer reconciles. The lib/news.ts FAQ for this slug ('second full financial year ... first where the FY2026-27 threshold ... interact') contradicts itself on the same point.

Population claim with no figure, and this article's sources (ATO compulsory repayments, ATO thresholds) do not cite a debtor count. The 3.2 million figure appears only in the sources for the 20% cut article.
constants: HECS_HELP_2025_26.minimumThreshold and HECS_HELP_2025_26.bands in lib/constants/australian-tax.ts (line 476 onward); FY2026-27 is HECS_HELP.minimumThreshold (line 462)
reviewerNotes: I endorse the writer's main fact question. Returns lodged at tax time 2026 reconcile FY2025-26 income ($67,000 threshold). The page applies FY2026-27 $69,528 bands throughout: the lead, key facts, the $80,000 example ($10,472 excess, about $1,571) and the two-jobs paragraph. The fix belongs in the source and constants, not in this prose pass.

claims: The $80,000 worked example: excess $10,472, repayment about $1,571, $30/week STSL (about $1,560) 'within a few dollars'.
whys: If the tax-time year is corrected to FY2025-26 ($67,000 threshold), the excess becomes $13,000 and the repayment about $1,950. The $30/week STSL figure would then no longer reconcile, so the whole example has to be recomputed from constants, not patched.

claims: Division 296 tax, an extra 15% on earnings from balances above $3 million, applies from the same date.
whys: The figures are correct, but the sentence leaves out the extra 10% tier above $10 million that DIVISION_296 holds (veryLargeBalanceThreshold, additionalRate). Readers with very large balances get only part of the rule.

The writer flagged this and I confirm it: DIVISION_296 in lib/constants/super-contributions.ts (lines 201-208) also holds veryLargeBalanceThreshold 10,000,000 with additionalRate 0.10, and this sentence leaves that tier out.

claims: lifted the national minimum wage by 6%
whys: The exact figure is 5.97% ($24.95 to $26.44). The rounding is consistent across the headline, the title and the key facts '+6%' (line 18). Listed only so a reviewer can decide whether a YMYL page should show the exact figure.

claims: If your pay cycle runs Wednesday to Tuesday, the new rate begins on the first Wednesday in July: your first full July payslip may still show a few days at the old rate.
whys: 1 July 2026 is itself a Wednesday. A Wednesday-to-Tuesday cycle therefore starts the new rate on 1 July, and no July pay period carries days at the old rate. The example needs a different start day (for example Monday). The lib/news.ts FAQ answer uses the same Wednesday example.
constants: Example text only; first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026

claims: On a $52,254.80 annual income ... the Medicare levy is shaded rather than charged in full, because earnings sit close to the low-income threshold.
whys: The singles shade-in band ends at $35,013, so the full 2% levy applies at $52,254.80. The page's own $7,025 annual tax only reconciles with the full levy: 6,196.44 bracket tax, minus 216.18 LITO, plus 1,045.10 full Medicare levy, equals 7,025.36. Line 30 ('the shaded Medicare levy') and the lib/news.ts FAQ answer ('Medicare levy shading') repeat the same error.
constants: Medicare levy low-income thresholds / shade-in upper bound (singles $28,011 to $35,013) in the tax constants
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's factQuestions are valid and left the text unchanged per the rules. The 'shaded Medicare levy' claim at $52,254.80 is wrong because the full 2% applies. 'Very little' taxed at 30% is misleading. 'Your figures will differ if you have a study loan' conflicts with the HECS section. The Wednesday pay-cycle example fails because 1 July 2026 is a Wednesday. The population claims and the $450m costing also remain on the writer's list.

claims: A full-time minimum-wage income sits only just above that $45,000 mark, so very little of it is taxed at the higher 30% rate.
whys: $7,254.80 is taxed at 30%. That produces about $2,176 of the $6,196 bracket tax (around a third), so 'very little' misleads the reader.

claims: Your figures will differ if you have a study loan, salary sacrifice arrangements or additional income.
whys: This contradicts the HECS section at line 111, which says the take-home figures apply whether or not you carry a HECS-HELP debt, because $52,254.80 is below the $69,528 threshold. A study loan changes the figures only when combined with other income.
